claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (founder, Bloom Nutrition) states that the primary value of private jet travel for business operators is not the in-flight experience but the elimination of airport overhead: skipping airport check-in, security, and terminal time removes hours from a trip that commercial travel would require.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: Trip is short enough that in-flight time is a minor portion of total travel time
Private FBO terminal replaces commercial airport
claims.mechanism: Commercial air travel requires arriving 60-90 minutes before departure for check-in, security, and boarding; private FBO allows drive-up-to-plane boarding with no queue, compressing pre-flight time to near zero.
bounded_by: Applies to routes where airport overhead is a large share of door-to-door time; less relevant for long-haul flights where in-flight time dominates

examples.text: Greg LaVecchia describes a trip with Leo (President of Bloom Nutrition) and a cameraman (JJ) aboard a Citation CJ2 six-seater private jet. The car pulled up directly to the plane; they walked on immediately. LaVecchia emphasizes that the biggest advantage was not the aircraft itself but bypassing the commercial airport entirely, which he says removes hours from travel and gives full control over departure and arrival timing.

practices.text: When evaluating private air travel for business use, prioritize the time saved by eliminating airport overhead (check-in, security, boarding queues) rather than focusing on in-flight comfort or aircraft size.
